summary: Virtual positioning of a sound emitter (ls::SoundTransformSystem::ProcessNewVirtualPositioningComponents / ProcessVirtualPositionedSounds, which also use SoundRoomStateComponent): the emitter's own position and two copies of the virtual (room-portal) position.

fields.name: Position
fields.evidence: Toolkit ctor ls::SoundVirtualPositionComponent(Vector3f const&, Vector3f const&) (GameEngine.dll+0x68F410) stores the first argument at +0; live: a distinct value per instance (emitter positions), NaN/FLT_MAX defaults. Windows creator bg3.exe+0x3EA5C90 (ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw(.., 0x24, ..)) copies its first Vector3f argument here as 8 + 4 bytes. Some live instances hold 0xFFC00000 (a NaN default of the caller) - the raw check's 'not an ordinary float' is that NaN, not a wrong type.

fields.name: VirtualPosition
fields.evidence: Same ctor stores the second argument at +0x0C and again at +0x18; live +0x0C..+0x17 and +0x18..+0x23 hold the same 9 values. Windows creator bg3.exe+0x3EA5C90 copies its second Vector3f argument to +0x0C (8 + 4 bytes).

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: Initialised from the same argument as +0x0C (ctor); probably the previous/target virtual position used for interpolation. Windows creator bg3.exe+0x3EA5C90 copies the same second argument again to +0x18 (8 + 4 bytes); size 0x24 ends here.

open_questions: Role of the third vector (+0x18): initialised like +0x0C; whether it is the previous or the target virtual position was not read from the parallel jobs of ProcessVirtualPositionedSounds.
second_pass: Offsets and widths confirmed on Windows by the creator bg3.exe+0x3EA5C90 (AllocRaw 0x24; three 12-byte vectors from two Vector3f arguments), matching the Toolkit constructor. The failed raw check was a NaN (0xFFC00000) default in live data.
